item.description: it’s a pity. [NOTES: corrected to ‘miastadh’.]
it’s a pity.
cut into small pieces. Mixed with butter and heated. Used to heal cuts.
a yellow flower. The root of the ‘cairt shleamhna’ was obtained from this flower. This root was used for tarring nets. Left them soft and supple. Also used as a poultice.
[See barra-braoinain.]
bramble leaves. Used as a poultice to take thorns out of fingers, skin.
used for poultice. [NOTES: ‘phadruig’ corrected to ‘phàdruig’.]
making an onset, attack. As in an argument. [NOTES: note added – ‘Rinn e starragan air.’]
a film on calm water.
phosphorescence. [NOTES: note added – usually means ‘jelly-fish’.]
will o’ the wisp.
partition. [NOTES: ‘callabho’ corrected to ‘calabhò’.]
a hammer with a square head and round head. Used by a shoemaker.
warring hammer.
washer.
a beauty as in a good joke.
supports below the seat in a boat.
tummers of a boat. From the keel up to the seats.
the traveller that went up and down the mast. [NOTES: “a’” put in brackets.]
a constable.
bung in a boat.
where you gripped the oars. [NOTES: ‘raimh’ corrected to ‘ràimh’.]
the point of a sail. [NOTES: corrected to ‘pìc’.]
an extra seat at the back or front of a boat.
applied to all sort of water that would accumulate in a boat. [NOTES: note added – variant of ‘taoim’.]
applied to water that was left overnight with fish in that water. [NOTES: ‘ghròd’ corrected to ‘ghrod’.]
the rope between the buoy and the float rope. [NOTES: corrected to ‘ribe’.]
a gut made from a horse’s [sic] or mane.
home-made fishing flies. Made from the feathers of a swan or from dog’s hairs. [NOTES: note added above ‘maghraichean’ – maghair.]
a buoy made from a dog’s pelt. [NOTES: ‘buthta’ corrected to ‘buta’ and a note added above ‘coinnaice’ – consheice.]
getting yourself in shape, order.
a year old female sheep. [NOTES: corrected to ‘dianag’.]
applied to a sheep over five years of age. [NOTES: corrected to ‘crog’.]
a sheep without milk or without a lamb. [NOTES: ‘sheisg’ corrected to ‘sheasg’.]
applied to a ram with one testicle.
a ram without testicles.
a normal ram.
pet lamb.
a form of pneumonia which could kill a sheep.
similarly affecting the kidneys but not so deadly as the above illness [i.e. crith-sgamhain (q.v.)]. [NOTES: ‘airnean’ corrected to ‘àirnean’.]
tickbone [tick-borne?] fever. [NOTES: corrected to ‘fiabhras-a’-ghartain’.]
